t: Classical Photonic Computer: Fiber Loss Budget — Simple
name: Classical Photonic Computer: Fiber Loss Budget — Simple

description:

t: Classical Photonic Computer: Signal Index Desk — Simple
name: Classical Photonic Computer: Signal Index Desk — Simple
title: Classical Photonic Computer: Signal Index Desk — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] The signal index is the SNR: the desk computes it from the received power and the noise — shot, thermal, and amplifier. The index decides the modulation order: 20 dB carries 64-QAM, 10 dB carries QPSK — the math assigns the format.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: SNR: 1 mW received, 10 µW noise = 20.0 dB. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.

real_world_basis: SNR-based format assignment is the real basis of coherent optics.
signature_version: Signature version: the fixed-signal index desk — the chapter's Fixed Signal Index as the stability target, with the manifestation framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: the noise must include the amplifier — the link's NF is the noise.
math_note: SNR: 1 mW received, 10 µW noise: 20.0 dB [verified]; Shannon capacity at 50 GHz, 20 dB SNR: 332910.6 Mbps [verified]

math_check.note: corrected 2026-10-19: arg was 50 MHz against a 50 GHz label; 332.9 Gbps

safety: No hazard; the failure mode is a format assigned from transmit power.
how_it_works: Compute the received power, sum the noise sources, and take the ratio. The demo indexes three links.
